newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SMH CEO sees higher 1997 profit, sales.
newsitem.headline: SMH CEO sees higher 1997 profit, sales.

text.p: Nicolas Hayek, chairman and chief executive of Swiss watchmaker Ste Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie SA (SMH), said he expected an increase in 1997 sales and profits from 1996.

After completion of the first quarter, "we will have a better year than in 1996 if there is no major upset with currencies and business during Christmas is as normal," Hayek told Reuters in an interview.
Asked if he was referring to profits and sales in the forecast, Hayek said: "Yes."

Hayek, however, cautioned against excessive optimism, noting the most important months for SMH are from August to November and in 1996 dampened consumption during the last four months had lead to a disappointment.
"We are confident that this will be a good year for SMH," Hayek said, adding: "Practically all brands are selling well, all are making progress."
He said the watch fair in Basle had been very positive and last year's necessary investments in Asia would not burden this year's result as much as last year.
The current exchange rates "certainly improve our situation by three to seven percent," Hayek said, referring to SMH's sales.
In Japan, however, Hayek said the currency situation was the reverse.
So far Hayek has only forecast that 1997 would be a good year.
SMH's 1996 net profit rose to a preliminary 282 million Swiss francs from 273 million in 1995.
